sections.overview: The inventory name Crenicichla johanna is the familiar historical combination; a phylogenetic revision now places the species in Lugubria as Lugubria johanna.
sections.identification: It is a large-bodied pike cichlid; in the revised genus Lugubria, L. johanna is one of the exceptions lacking the usual dark caudal-fin blotch.
sections.habitat: Its reported range spans several cis-Andean South American drainages, including the Amazon, Orinoco and Guiana systems, though the name may cover multiple lineages.
sections.diet: Like other pike cichlids it is predatory, but species-level field records do not justify a precise prey list across its entire broad range.
sections.behavior: It belongs to the robust-bodied Lugubria lineage of pike cichlids, a group separated from several other former Crenicichla lineages by phylogenetic evidence.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted do not provide a dependable species-specific account of its breeding cycle or parental care.
sections.ecology: The old name Crenicichla johanna is still useful for finding earlier literature; compare the catalogue’s Crenicichla strigata profile, another species now assigned to Lugubria.
sections.conservation: A cited regional survey and the global assessment report it as Least Concern, but the species-complex evidence cautions against treating all records as one uniform population.
